title: Travel on a Budget
summary: Ama and Carlos share simple ways to travel cheaply without missing the best parts of a trip.

cover.scene: Flat 2D illustration: Ama and Carlos at a small table with a map, a backpack and a train ticket, bright window behind them, no text

sentences.text: Welcome back, everyone! Today we are talking about travelling on a budget.
I love this topic. Last summer I visited three countries for very little money.
How did you do that? Flights are so expensive!
I booked my tickets early and I chose the cheapest days to travel.
Smart. I usually check the prices every morning for a week.
Also, I stayed in a hostel instead of a hotel, and I met lots of interesting people.
Was it noisy at night?
Sometimes, but I took earplugs, so it was not a big problem.
And what about food? Restaurants can cost a fortune.
I bought fresh bread and fruit at the local market, and it was delicious.

quiz.q: When did Ama book her tickets?

quiz.explain: I stayed in a hostel instead of a hotel.
I bought fresh bread and fruit at the local market.

sentences.text: Now, what about getting around once you arrive?
I walk as much as I can, because it is free and you see more of the city.
For longer trips, I take the train or the bus instead of a taxi.
Good idea. Many cities also sell a cheap pass for all public transport.
Yes, and some museums are free on certain days.
Do you always follow a strict plan?
No, I keep some free time, because the best moments are often a surprise.
I agree. One evening I followed a small street to a tiny square full of music.
That sounds wonderful. So, the main message is to plan a little and stay flexible.
Exactly. Thanks for listening, and have a safe trip!
